content.thinking:
I should avoid restating the specific impact figures I was given as if I'd computed them myself, and shouldn't invent my own numbers either — better to describe the effect qualitatively and note the rough duration of the incident when writing the root cause and executive summary.

I need to flag key assumptions clearly: that the deployment caused the incident is inferred from timing correlation plus the fact that reverting fixed it, that I haven't verified actual customer impact beyond the metrics shown, that the log sample only covers a short window, and that the specific error is presumably tied to missing data rather than confirmed — which should be stated as speculation, not fact.

assumptions: The flag is treated as the cause on the strength of timing correlation plus a successful revert; no code-level reproduction of the ZeroDivisionError was performed during the incident.
Impact is assumed limited to the account page, based on the error logs read; no other endpoint was explicitly checked.
Only the 8 minutes of logs before 21:40 and one production change record were reviewed, so earlier or unrelated contributing changes cannot be fully excluded.
Recovery is judged from service metrics returning to baseline, not from any direct confirmation that shoppers could load the page again.
Why the division denominator was zero (e.g. accounts with no spend history) was not established during the incident.
input.executive_summary: On 28 September 2026, a change was switched on that broke the account page of the online shop. Shoppers who tried to view their account between 21:35 and 21:41 UTC saw errors instead of the page; browsing and other parts of the shop were unaffected. The problem began as the change was rolled out to all traffic and lasted about six minutes. Automated monitoring raised an alert at 21:40, the cause was traced to the newly enabled change within a minute, and it was switched back off at 21:41. The service was confirmed back to its normal behaviour at 21:42. A draft code change has since been opened to fix the underlying defect so the feature can be safely re-enabled.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was rolled out from 0% to 100% between 21:35 and 21:36, exposing an unguarded division in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47` that raised `ZeroDivisionError` on the account page request path; every request that evaluated the flag as on and hit that path failed. Latency and CPU/memory stayed flat throughout, ruling out a resource or traffic cause, and turning the flag back off returned the service to baseline, which confirms the flag as the trigger.
